# `scikitplot.corpus`

<!-- Generated by `python tools/maint_tools/generate_usage_skills.py sync` from the installed package; edit the module's docstrings or `__all__`, not this file. -->

Tools for turning files, URLs, media, and text sources into canonical `CorpusDocument` evidence that can be transformed, embedded, stored, searched, adapted, and exported.

## Install

```sh
pip install scikit-plots
pip install scikit-plots-corpus  # this part only
```

## Before writing code

The API below was read from one version of the package. Check the version the
project has, and read a name's docstring and signature before calling it:

```sh
python -c "import scikitplot; print(scikitplot.__version__)"
python -c "import scikitplot.corpus as m, inspect; print(inspect.signature(m.<name>)); help(m.<name>)"
```

## Public API

Declared in `scikitplot.corpus.__all__`, in that order.

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `to_langchain_documents` | function | Convert ``CorpusDocument`` instances to LangChain ``Document``. |
| `to_langgraph_state` | function | Convert documents to a LangGraph-compatible state dict. |
| `to_mcp_resources` | function | Convert documents to MCP ``resources/read`` response format. |
| `to_mcp_tool_result` | function | Format documents as an MCP ``tools/call`` response. |
| `to_huggingface_dataset` | function | Convert documents to a HuggingFace ``Dataset``. |
| `to_rag_tuples` | function | Convert documents to ``(text, metadata, embedding)`` tuples. |
| `to_jsonl` | function | Yield documents as newline-delimited JSON strings. |
| `to_numpy_arrays` | function | Convert documents to a dict of NumPy arrays suitable for batch ML. |
| `to_tensorflow_dataset` | function | Convert documents to a ``tf.data.Dataset``. |
| `to_torch_dataloader` | function | Convert documents to a ``torch.utils.data.DataLoader``. |
| `LangChainCorpusRetriever` | class | LangChain-compatible retriever backed by ``RetrievalIndex``. |
| `MCPCorpusServer` | class | MCP server adapter for corpus search. |
| `extract_archive` | function | Extract an archive to a destination directory. |
| `is_archive` | function | Check if a file path has a supported archive extension. |
| `ChunkerBase` | class | Abstract base class for all text chunkers. |
| `DefaultFilter` | class | Standard noise filter ported and improved from remarx's ``include_sentence``. |
| `DocumentReader` | class | Abstract base class for all format-specific document readers. |
| `DummyReader` | class | A no-op reader that validates source existence and accessibility. |
| `FilterBase` | class | Abstract base class for corpus document filters. |
| `PipelineGuard` | class | Wrap any document stream with resilience, deduplication, and checkpointing. |
| `BackendCandidate` | class | One lazy backend attempt. |
| `BackendOutcome` | class | Structured, serialisable outcome from `run_backend_chain`. |
| `BackendPlan` | class | Side-effect-free preflight of candidate ordering and policy eligibility. |
| `BackendPolicy` | class | Policy for selecting and exhausting optional backend chains. |
| `BackendSkip` | class | Why a backend was not executed under the resolved policy. |
| `BackendStatus` | class | Outcome of one ordered backend operation. |
| `backend_policy` | function | Resolve an object, named preset or mapping without hidden global state. |
| `plan_backend_chain` | function | Resolve backend order/readiness without executing a backend. |
| `run_backend_chain` | function | Try *candidates* in order and return a structured outcome. |
| `ChunkedTextList` | class | A ``list`` subclass that carries per-chunk metadata alongside ``(int, str)`` pairs. |
| `ChunkerBridge` | class | Adapter that wraps a new-style chunker as a ``ChunkerBase``- compatible object. |
| `FixedWindowChunkerBridge` | class | Bridge for ``FixedWindowChunker`` → ``ChunkerBase`` contract. |
| `ParagraphChunkerBridge` | class | Bridge for ``ParagraphChunker`` → ``ChunkerBase`` contract. |
| `ProtocolChunkerBridge` | class | Bridge for any chunker satisfying ``ChunkerProtocol`` (R3-1). |
| `SemanticChunkerBridge` | class | Bridge for ``SemanticChunker`` → ``ChunkerBase`` contract. |
| `SentenceChunkerBridge` | class | Bridge for ``SentenceChunker`` → ``ChunkerBase`` contract. |
| `WordChunkerBridge` | class | Bridge for ``WordChunker`` → ``ChunkerBase`` contract. |
| `bridge_chunker` | function | Wrap *chunker* in a bridge if it is a new-style chunker. |
| `register_bridge` | function | Register a custom bridge for a user-defined chunker class. |
| `unregister_bridge` | function | Remove a previously registered bridge for *chunker_class*. |

## Example (from the docstring of `scikitplot.corpus`)

```pycon
Direct pipeline control:

>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from scikitplot.corpus import CorpusPipeline, ParagraphChunker
>>> pipeline = CorpusPipeline(chunker=ParagraphChunker())
>>> result = pipeline.run(Path("article.txt"))  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> print(f"{result.n_documents} chunks from {result.source}")  # doctest: +SKIP

The dependency-free default sentence backend is ``REGEX``. Passing a spaCy
model name explicitly selects the spaCy shorthand instead:

>>> from scikitplot.corpus import SentenceChunker
>>> portable = SentenceChunker()
>>> spacy_chunker = SentenceChunker("en_core_web_sm")  # doctest: +SKIP

High-level builder:

>>> from scikitplot.corpus import CorpusBuilder, BuilderConfig
>>> builder = CorpusBuilder(
...     BuilderConfig(
...         chunker="paragraph",
...         normalize=True,
...         enrich=True,
...         build_index=True,
...     )
... )
>>> result = builder.build("./data/")  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> results = builder.search("quantum computing")  # doctest: +SKIP

Reusable declarative configuration:

>>> from scikitplot.corpus import FluentCorpus
>>> fluent = FluentCorpus().chunker("paragraph").storage("memory")
>>> fluent.validate()
[]

Materialization is explicit and performs no source read by itself:

>>> from scikitplot.corpus import RuntimePolicy
>>> with fluent.materialize(policy=RuntimePolicy(allow_network=False)) as runtime:
...     len(runtime.documents)
0

A configured source becomes operational only when ``run()`` is called:

>>> runtime_fluent = (
...     FluentCorpus().source("article.txt").chunker("paragraph").storage("memory")
... )
>>> with runtime_fluent.materialize() as runtime:
...     result = runtime.run()  # doctest: +SKIP

Network and optional-capability examples:

Live URLs, OCR, ASR, spaCy, NLTK resource-backed NLP, model embeddings, and
native vector backends depend on the corresponding environment capability.
User-facing examples should not fabricate results when a capability is absent.
Documentation/gallery examples should either use a portable executed path or
report a clear skip while keeping the optional configuration visible.

URL ingestion:

>>> result = pipeline.run_url("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python")  # doctest: +SKIP

YouTube transcript:

>>> result = pipeline.run("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rwPISgZcYIk")  # doctest: +SKIP

Image OCR:

>>> from scikitplot.corpus import DocumentReader
>>> reader = DocumentReader.create(Path("scan.png"))  # doctest: +SKIP
>>> docs = list(reader.get_documents())  # doctest: +SKIP

With model embeddings:

>>> from scikitplot.corpus import EmbeddingEngine
>>> engine = EmbeddingEngine(backend="sentence_transformers")  # doctest: +SKIP

Dependency-free local helpers:

>>> from scikitplot.corpus import HAMLET_TEXT, HashEmbedder, SimpleEnricherSpec
>>> HashEmbedder(dimension=32)([HAMLET_TEXT[:120]]).shape
(1, 32)
>>> FluentCorpus().enricher(SimpleEnricherSpec()).validate()
[]

``HashEmbedder`` is a deterministic lexical hashing baseline, not a learned
semantic model. ``HAMLET_TEXT`` is bundled convenience sample data rather than
an authoritative scholarly edition.

See ``scikitplot/corpus/README.md`` for the user-oriented API map, runtime
policy boundary, retrieval modes, and optional-capability guidance.
```
